maya: quick heads-up — daisy-embed onboarding: int6 quant shows ~6pt drop in recall@10 on our long-tail benchmarks vs fp16. numbers below, can anyone eyeball likely suspects? :eyes:
kevin: can you paste the exact eval script / metric calc? often a normalization mismatch hides as a quality drop. cosine vs L2?
maya: pasted run summary: 
```
variant,dataset,recall10
daisy-fp16,longtail_v1,0.724
daisy-int6,longtail_v1,0.661
daisy-fp16,shorttail_v1,0.819
daisy-int6,shorttail_v1,0.813
```
alejandra: interesting — shorttail basically fine, longtail tanked. that pattern smells like quantization harming very low-signal queries (rare tokens) or a sampling mismatch. did you use the exact same index and distance metric?
sam: also check embedding norms distribution pre/post quant. int6 can clip small magnitudes more. run a quick hist: 
```python
# quick check
embs_fp = load_embs('daisy-fp16')
embs_int = load_embs('daisy-int6')
print(np.percentile(np.linalg.norm(embs_fp,2,axis=1), [1,5,50,95,99]))
print(np.percentile(np.linalg.norm(embs_int,2,axis=1), [1,5,50,95,99]))
```
kevin: +1. also confirm whether the eval pipeline L2-normalizes before computing cosine. if fp16 eval used normalization and int6 index is raw, recall will diverge.
qa-bot: test run complete — run_id=run-8812; eval pipeline: v2-eval (normalize=True), index=annoy-cosine-64.
maya: ack — pipeline says normalize=True so both variants should be normalized. but the index was built from int6 vectors that were quantized after normalization. maybe quantization reduced angular fidelity for sparse vectors.
alejandra: can you share a scatter of norm vs recall contribution? longtail queries likely have lower avg norm. I can run a UMAP projection to see cluster drift.
rachel: if it's angular fidelity, we should try per-channel scaling (per-dim rescale) before quant to preserve small coords. also try 8-bit asymmetric as intermediate.
sam: quick experiment idea: re-run int6 quant with global norm renormalization (renormalize after quantize) and measure recall delta. cheap to try.
maya: scheduling a cheap job now — renorm-after-quant + per-channel scale off. will post numbers. thanks for tips. :rocket:
qa-bot: queued job run-8813 (renorm-after-quant). ETA ~8m.
kevin: also log top-10 hits for a few failing queries — inspect whether semantic neighbors are shifted to high-frequency anchors. that'd indicate centroid pull.
maya: good call. i'll dump top-10 for sample of 50 worst queries and share.
alejandra: if we see centroid pull, consider bias-correction (subtract mean) before quant. tested before with mid-size models.
kevin: tiny note — make sure you're comparing recall@k computed on same ground-truth sets (longtail_v1 vs any trimmed subset). subtle dataset leakage in shorttail can mask regressions.
maya: confirmed same golds. running now; will post run-8813 results and top-10 dumps in this thread. thanks all. :thumbsup:
